top_strength: Jack built real trust by making the pricing transparent and actionable — he broke the quote into two concrete scenarios ("$3,640" for a full pack day vs. "$2,860" for a 4-hour partial pack) and proactively steered her toward the cheaper option that matched what she'd actually described needing, which is exactly the kind of budget-conscious framing that earns repeat callbacks like this one.
coaching_note: You're clear and transparent on pricing, but you skipped the two things that move the needle most: the Save Your Ass prep speech (zero mention of consolidation or carload tips) and the differentiators — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee — none of which came up. You also never used her name once even after spelling it out, and you let the call end without checking a move date or asking her to book today. Build a mental checklist so the close isn't just "send the quote and wait" — always attempt to schedule, always run the differentiators, always drop the prep speech before you hang up.
phone_presence_notes: Casual, consistently warm language ("Cool," "For sure," "Gotcha") kept the customer comfortable and she closed the call clearly satisfied, thanking him twice and calling the breakdown "super helpful."
